correctness.rationale: Fourier diagonalization yields kernel F_n(s,j) with ρkn=16n⁴ sin⁴(πk/n), and continuum H_s=1+2Σ exp(−16π⁴sk⁴)cos(2πkx). For σ=1/3000, first-frequency weighted domination shows continuum antipode unique minimum and h(s)=H_s(1/2) has unique zero s* in (σ,1/1500), D=h'(s*)>0. Discrete tail bounds ρkn≥256k⁴ imply, for sufficiently large n, antipodal spatial minimum for every s≥σ and monotonic crossing; this is the eventual, not first, sign-change time. Uniform expansion ρkn=c k⁴(1−2π²k²/(3n²)+O(k⁴n⁻⁴)) gives τn/n⁴=s*−G/(Dn²)+O(n⁻⁴) even and s*−(G+B/8)/(Dn²)+O(n⁻⁴) odd; half-grid sampling causes odd correction. Independent Fourier/direct numerical checks for even/odd n through 321 matched coefficients and sign, not universal proof. No explicit finite n0 is claimed.
